facts.content: Patient has central chest pressure lasting for 2 hours.
facts.source_text: CC: Central chest pressure x2 hrs, began while gardening

facts.content: The chest pain began while gardening.
The chest pain is described as 'someone sitting on chest' and is constant.
Pain radiates to the left arm and shoulder.
Associated symptoms include shortness of breath, diaphoresis, nausea without vomiting, and palpitations.
facts.source_text: Assoc: SOB, diaphoresis, nausea (no emesis), palpitations

facts.content: This is the first episode of such symptoms, which are ongoing during the call.
facts.source_text: First episode; sx ongoing during call

facts.content: Patient has a history of hypertension.
Patient is allergic to aspirin, causing mild swelling.
Patient's father had a fatal myocardial infarction at around 60 years old.
Patient's mother has heart disease.
Patient smokes 10 cigarettes per day for 15 years.
Patient consumes about 7 to 8 pints of beer per week.
Patient is sedentary, overweight, lives alone, and is a restaurant owner.
facts.source_text: sedentary; overweight; lives alone; restaurant owner

facts.content: Chest pain with classic acute coronary syndrome features needs rule-out for acute myocardial infarction.
facts.source_text: Chest pain w/ classic ACS features—r/o AMI

facts.content: Patient has essential hypertension.
Patient has tobacco use disorder.
Patient is overweight or possibly obese.
Patient has a non-anaphylactic allergy to aspirin.
Patient to be transported to the emergency department by EMS with continuous monitoring en route.
facts.source_text: EMS transport to ED; continuous monitoring en route

facts.content: Perform STAT ECG, cardiac enzymes, and chest X-ray on arrival.
facts.source_text: STAT ECG, cardiac enzymes, CXR on arrival

facts.content: Consider aspirin 300 mg if benefit outweighs risk, document allergy, and prepare for reaction management.
facts.source_text: Consider aspirin 300 mg if benefit > risk; document allergy, prepare for reaction mgmt

facts.content: Start oxygen, IV access, nitrates, and morphine as needed for pain if blood pressure allows.
facts.source_text: Start O₂, IV access, nitrates & morphine PRN pain if BP allows

facts.content: Administer antiplatelet or anticoagulation per ACS protocol using clopidogrel or heparin.
Admit to cardiology if acute coronary syndrome is confirmed, consider cath lab.
facts.source_text: Admit to cardiology if ACS confirmed; consider cath lab

facts.content: Manage hypertension per emergency department protocols.
Counsel on smoking cessation, weight control, and moderate alcohol consumption post-acute phase.
facts.source_text: Counsel: smoking cessation, wt control, mod etOH (post-acute)
